texts.preamble: Del Monte Foods Private Limited vs Additional District Magistrate Budgam ... on 2 March, 2024 Author: Wasim Sadiq Nargal Bench: Wasim Sadiq Nargal Serial No. 153 Supplementary Causelist-I High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh At S`Rinagar Cm(835/2024) In Wp(C) 2883/2023 Cm(6853/2023) Cm(6854/2023) Cm(736/2024) Del Monte Foods Private Limited. ...Petitioner(s) Through: None. Vs. Additional District Magistrate Budgam & ...Respondent(s) Others. Through: Mr. Satinder Singh Kala, Aag. Coram:
texts.arguments: Mr. Satinder Singh Kala, the learned Additional Advocate General submits that the Government has issued a notification dated 15th December, 2023, being S.O 616, in exercise of the power conferred under sub-section (3) of Section 70 of the Food Safety & Standards, Act 2006 read with Rule 3.2.1 of the Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011 and accordingly, appointed the following Presiding Officers for Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Kashmir and Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Jammu: Jurisdiction Presiding Officer Kashmir Shri. Shujat Al Khan S/O Usman Ali Khan R/O Village Naloosa, Tehsil Boniyar Sub Del Monte Foods Private Limited vs Additional District Magistrate Budgam ... on 2 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77561614/ 1 Division Uri, District Baramulla. Jammu Shri Ramesh Kumar Wattal S/O Lt. Shri Jagar Nath Wattal R/O House No. 69, Durga Nagar Enclave Sector,1 Jammu. Mr. Satinder Singh Kala, the learned Additional Advocate General submits that in the light of the notification issued by the Government, this Court lacks inherent jurisdiction to adjudicate the instant writ petition any further and as such, the instant writ petition needs to be transferred to the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Kashmir, for adjudication. He further submits that the petitioner has to approach the said Tribunal by way of an appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety & Standards, Act 2006 against the order of the Adjudicating Officer, which is under challenge in the present writ petition.

Mr. Satinder Singh Kala, the learned Additional Advocate General submits that in the light of the notification issued by the Government, this Court lacks inherent jurisdiction to adjudicate the instant writ petition any further and as such, the instant writ petition needs to be transferred to the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Kashmir, for adjudication. He further submits that the petitioner has to approach the said Tribunal by way of an appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety & Standards, Act 2006 against the order of the Adjudicating Officer, which is under challenge in the present writ petition.
